requirement: REL-1 — the physical two-machine demonstration; the viewer's broadcast freshness within 5 seconds
method: The browser's DOM carries a MutationObserver installed on the viewer's message list; it records the wall-clock instant each message card FIRST appears (a per-sequence set, so a catch-up page is recorded once and a live SSE frame is recorded at its arrival). The sender records the instant the server acknowledged its send (the api-client's own clock, immediately after the committed answer). The difference is the viewer's freshness.

same_clock_measurement.why: the sender and the viewer are the SAME machine (NSG-Mac-mini.local), so the difference carries NO clock-skew term at all
same_clock_measurement.sender: CLAUDE-MAC-1 (the Mac installation of the frozen portable package)
same_clock_measurement.verdict: pass — 0.150 s against the 5 s bound

cross_machine_measurement.why: the sender is the OTHER physical machine (ngs-staging), so the two clocks differ; the offset is measured, not assumed
cross_machine_measurement.sender: CLAUDE-STAGING-1 (the staging installation of the frozen Claude Code package)
cross_machine_measurement.clock_offset_method: the server's HTTP Date header is the common reference: 9 samples per client, the median of (client midpoint - server epoch). The header has 1-second resolution, so each median carries about +/-450 ms of quantization uncertainty, and the DIFFERENCE of the two medians inherits up to about +/-900 ms from that term alone, before any network asymmetry.
cross_machine_measurement.arithmetic: elapsed = (viewer_clock - mac_offset) - (sender_clock - staging_offset) = raw_difference + (staging_offset - mac_offset) = 172 + 104 = 276 ms
cross_machine_measurement.reported_as: 0.276 s (the corrected cross-machine freshness), with up to about +/-0.9 s of clock-offset uncertainty from the 1-second-resolution Date header.
cross_machine_measurement.verdict: pass — 0.276 s corrected (raw 0.172 s) against the 5 s bound

honest_limits: The measured interval is sender-acknowledgement -> DOM card insertion, not send-start -> painted pixel. The acknowledgement is after the commit and the observer fires before the paint, so the interval is not the whole user-perceived latency.

The cross-machine number carries the clock-offset uncertainty stated above (each offset median has about +/-450 ms of quantization; their difference up to about +/-900 ms). The same-clock number carries no clock term at all.

Only seq 3 and seq 4 are the freshness canaries; the two conversation broadcasts (seq 1, seq 2) are recorded with their live DOM arrival instants too, but no sender-acknowledgement instant was paired with them.
